newsitem.title: UK: Citibank to build UK headquarters in Canary Wharf.
newsitem.headline: Citibank to build UK headquarters in Canary Wharf.

text.p: Citibank has exchanged contracts with Canary Wharf Ltd for the building of a new 560,000 sq ft UK corporate front office building in the east London dockside development.
Canary Wharf said construction would start in early 1997 and was due for completion towards the end of 1999. The building, designed by Norman Foster, will be owned by Citibank.

"We are delighted that Citibank is to move to Canary Wharf. This is a rare opportunity for London to benefit from a fine new building by one of the world's greatest architects to be occupied by a global financial player," said George Iacobescu, deputy chief executive of Canary Wharf Ltd.

The deal coincides with the first anniversary of Canadian businessman Paul Reichmann's return to Canary Wharf as leader of the consortium of investors who bought the property development in December 1995 following its collapse in 1992.
Shareholders include Saudi Prince Waleed bin Abdul Aziz, CNA Financial Corporation, Mutual Series Fund and affiliates of Republic New York Corporation.
Completed buildings are currently over 80 percent leased and the working poulation is expected to rise from 15,000 to 20,000 during 1997, Canary Wharf Ltd said.
